newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on slack exports, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on slack exports, weather.

text.p: A bearish export scene knocked CBOT wheat futures to a lower close as did prospects for increased wheat selling soon due to improved weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
"There's no demand plus Argentina and Australia have big crops," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International. "In and of itself, wheat has no strength.
Bruce and others also said there was a significant amount of corn/wheat and soybean/wheat spreading Friday.
But the onus for the wheat market remained on the export picture which again dimmed overnight.
"There's been wheat business but not from the U.S., mainly Australian and French," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

European grain traders Friday said sales of 1.5 million tonnes of Australian wheat to Iran was done in the low $150.00s per tonne fob, and said Australia was best placed to grab further business with Iran this year because it enjoyed a quality advantage over other exporters.
There were other reminders of the slack export sales pace, the traders said.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to 6-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down 6-3/4 at $3.80-1/2.
The Canadian Wheat Board signed a letter of agreement to sell more than one million tonnes of wheat to Thai flour mills over the next five years.
Wheat futures also dropped on diminished concerns about cold weather damage to the U.S. winter wheat crop because of ample snow cover, the traders said.

March wheat reached a session low of $3.79-1/4 a bushel when sell stops were hit at midday at and slightly above the $3.80 mark. Early Friday first support in the March was at $3.83 and second support was at $3.75.
Technicians said the four- and 20-day moving averages early Friday looked bearish for the March contract but bullish for May and July.

Spread action featured SAK Futures bull spread of one million bushels of July/September at 3-1/2 cents, September and Prudential Securities did 300,000 bushels of the December/July at 13-1/2 cents, premium December, traders said.
Cargill Inc, Refco Inc and Dean Witter Reynolds each sold 1.5 million bushels of March, traders said. E.D. and F. Man International bought four million bushels of March, they said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, below the 17,449 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, Continental Grain bought 200 March $3.80 calls and bought 200 March $3.80 puts at 18-1/2 cents, traders said. Cargill Investor Services bought 200 March $4.0 calls at three cents and FIMAT Futures sold 200 March $3.90 puts at 15 cents, they said.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 8,500 contracts, above the 4,024 traded Thursday.
